sections.title: Route
sections.sub: Where you're going and the way there. Used by the route and CDU steps.

rows.label: Departure
rows.desc: The airport you depart from. Its weather is on the Weather page.

ofp.title: The airports are in the header
ofp.body: The header has the flight number, the airports, the route as filed, the distance and the times.
ofp.note: The header names both airports first, in ICAO codes.

rows.label: Destination
rows.desc: Where you plan to land.

ofp.title: The airports are in the header
ofp.body: The header has the flight number, the airports, the route as filed, the distance and the times.
ofp.note: The header names both airports first, in ICAO codes.

rows.label: Alternate
rows.desc: Where you'd divert if you couldn't land at the destination.

ofp.title: The alternate has its own section
ofp.body: The alternate section gives the alternate airport, the route there and the fuel to get there.
ofp.note: The header names the alternate too.

rows.label: Flight number
rows.desc: Your flight's number, as filed.

ofp.title: The flight number opens the header
ofp.body: The header has the flight number, the airports, the route as filed, the distance and the times.
ofp.note: It comes before the airports in most layouts.

rows.label: Route
rows.desc: The filed route from the SID to the arrival, as you enter it in the CDU.

ofp.title: The route is in the header
ofp.body: The header has the flight number, the airports, the route as filed, the distance and the times.
ofp.note: The route sits between the departure and the destination, each with its runway.

rows.label: Distance
rows.desc: Planned air distance, which allows for the wind.

ofp.title: The distance is in the header
ofp.body: The header has the flight number, the airports, the route as filed, the distance and the times.
ofp.note: Air distance allows for the winds along the route.

rows.label: Planned time
rows.desc: Planned time from takeoff to landing.

ofp.title: The planned time is in the header
ofp.body: The header has the flight number, the airports, the route as filed, the distance and the times.
ofp.note: Estimated time en route, from takeoff to landing.

sections.title: Fuel and weights
sections.sub: Numbers for the fuel and weight steps and the CDU's PERF INIT page.

rows.label: Block fuel
rows.desc: All the fuel on board before engine start.

ofp.title: Block fuel is in the fuel plan
ofp.body: The fuel plan lists each part of the fuel, then the total you board.
ofp.note: Block is the total: everything on board before engine start.

rows.label: Center tank
rows.desc: What's left after both wing tanks fill. The Center tank fuel step suggests its answer from this.

ofp.title: Block fuel is in the fuel plan
ofp.body: The fuel plan lists each part of the fuel, then the total you board.
ofp.note: The center tank takes what's left of the block fuel after both wing tanks fill.

rows.label: Trip fuel
rows.desc: Planned burn from takeoff to landing.

ofp.title: Trip fuel is in the fuel plan
ofp.body: The fuel plan lists each part of the fuel, then the total you board.
ofp.note: Trip is the burn from takeoff to landing.

rows.label: Reserves
rows.desc: Alternate plus final reserve: what must be left at landing.
rows.loc: Enter on the CDU › PERF INIT

ofp.title: Reserves are in the fuel plan
ofp.body: The fuel plan lists each part of the fuel, then the total you board.
ofp.note: Reserve is the final reserve; the alternate fuel is listed beside it.

rows.label: Taxi fuel
rows.desc: Planned burn before takeoff.

ofp.title: Taxi fuel is in the fuel plan
ofp.body: The fuel plan lists each part of the fuel, then the total you board.
ofp.note: Taxi is the planned burn before takeoff.

rows.label: Minimum takeoff fuel
rows.desc: The least fuel to start the takeoff with: trip, contingency, alternate and final reserve. Check you have at least this before takeoff.

ofp.title: Minimum takeoff fuel is in the fuel plan
ofp.body: The fuel plan lists each part of the fuel, then the total you board.
ofp.note: The least fuel to start the takeoff with.

rows.label: Zero fuel weight
rows.desc: The airplane's weight without fuel.
rows.loc: Enter on the CDU › PERF INIT

ofp.title: Zero fuel weight is in the weights section
ofp.body: The weights section gives the planned zero fuel, takeoff and landing weights.
ofp.note: Enter it in thousands, as the CDU takes it.

rows.label: ZFW CG
rows.desc: Center of gravity without fuel, used for takeoff trim.
rows.loc: Enter on the CDU › TAKEOFF REF

ofp.title: The CG is in the weights section
ofp.body: The weights section gives the planned zero fuel, takeoff and landing weights.
ofp.note: Some layouts print the CG beside the zero fuel weight.

rows.label: Passengers and cargo
rows.desc: Passengers and cargo, from the plan's load sheet.

ofp.title: The payload is in the weights section
ofp.body: The weights section gives the planned zero fuel, takeoff and landing weights.
ofp.note: Passengers, then cargo.

rows.label: Planned takeoff weight
rows.desc: Zero fuel weight plus fuel at takeoff, from the plan.
rows.loc: Enter on the CDU › PERF INIT

ofp.title: The takeoff weight is in the weights section
ofp.body: The weights section gives the planned zero fuel, takeoff and landing weights.
ofp.note: Cross-check it with the FMC's gross weight.

sections.title: Cruise and levels
sections.sub: Used by the climb, cruise and descent steps.

rows.label: Cruise level
rows.desc: The level you plan to cruise at.
rows.loc: Enter on the CDU › PERF INIT

ofp.title: Cost index and cruise level are in the header
ofp.body: The header gives the cruise level, the cost index, and the average wind and temperature for the flight.
ofp.note: The navigation log repeats the level and wind at each fix.

rows.label: Cost index
rows.desc: Trades fuel against time. Lower saves fuel.
rows.loc: Enter on the CDU › PERF INIT

ofp.title: Cost index and cruise level are in the header
ofp.body: The header gives the cruise level, the cost index, and the average wind and temperature for the flight.
ofp.note: The navigation log repeats the level and wind at each fix.

rows.label: Cruise wind
rows.desc: Average wind at cruise level, from the plan.
rows.loc: Enter on the CDU › PERF INIT

ofp.title: The average wind is in the header
ofp.body: The header has the flight number, the airports, the route as filed, the distance and the times.
ofp.note: Each fix's own wind is in the navigation log.

rows.label: ISA deviation
rows.desc: How much warmer (plus) or colder (minus) than standard the air is at cruise.
rows.loc: Enter on the CDU › PERF INIT

ofp.title: The ISA deviation is in the header
ofp.body: The header has the flight number, the airports, the route as filed, the distance and the times.
ofp.note: Plus is warmer than standard.

rows.label: Transition altitude
rows.desc: Where you set standard pressure on the way up.
rows.loc: Enter on the CDU › PERF INIT

ofp.title: The transition altitude is in the header
ofp.body: The header has the flight number, the airports, the route as filed, the distance and the times.
ofp.note: The departure airport's transition altitude.

rows.label: Transition level
rows.desc: Where you switch back to the local setting on the way down. Also on Approach.

ofp.title: The transition level is in the header
ofp.body: The header has the flight number, the airports, the route as filed, the distance and the times.
ofp.note: The destination's transition level.

sections.title: Clearance
sections.sub: What ATC cleared you to fly. The same fields as the flight strip.

rows.label: Runway
rows.desc: The runway you depart from.

ofp.title: Your clearance comes from ATC
ofp.body: The OFP shows what was planned and filed. ATC's clearance can differ, so enter what ATC gives you here.
ofp.note: The filed SID is first in the route. Check it against your clearance.

rows.label: SID
rows.desc: The departure procedure.

ofp.title: Your clearance comes from ATC
ofp.body: The OFP shows what was planned and filed. ATC's clearance can differ, so enter what ATC gives you here.
ofp.note: The filed SID is first in the route. Check it against your clearance.

rows.label: Transition
rows.desc: Where the SID joins your route.

ofp.title: Your clearance comes from ATC
ofp.body: The OFP shows what was planned and filed. ATC's clearance can differ, so enter what ATC gives you here.
ofp.note: The filed SID is first in the route. Check it against your clearance.

rows.label: Initial altitude
rows.desc: The altitude you're cleared to climb to first.

ofp.title: Your clearance comes from ATC
ofp.body: The OFP shows what was planned and filed. ATC's clearance can differ, so enter what ATC gives you here.
ofp.note: The filed SID is first in the route. Check it against your clearance.

rows.label: Squawk
rows.desc: Your transponder code.

ofp.title: Your squawk comes from ATC
ofp.body: The OFP shows what was planned and filed. ATC's clearance can differ, so enter what ATC gives you here.
ofp.note: The filed SID is first in the route. Check it against your clearance.

rows.label: Ground
rows.desc: For pushback and taxi.

ofp.title: Frequencies come from the chart and ATIS
ofp.body: The OFP shows what was planned and filed. ATC's clearance can differ, so enter what ATC gives you here.
ofp.note: The filed SID is first in the route. Check it against your clearance.

rows.label: Tower
rows.desc: For takeoff.

ofp.title: Frequencies come from the chart and ATIS
ofp.body: The OFP shows what was planned and filed. ATC's clearance can differ, so enter what ATC gives you here.
ofp.note: The filed SID is first in the route. Check it against your clearance.

rows.label: Departure frequency
rows.desc: The frequency to call after takeoff.

ofp.title: Frequencies come from the chart and ATIS
ofp.body: The OFP shows what was planned and filed. ATC's clearance can differ, so enter what ATC gives you here.
ofp.note: The filed SID is first in the route. Check it against your clearance.

rows.label: Note
rows.desc: Anything else ATC told you.

ofp.title: Your clearance comes from ATC
ofp.body: The OFP shows what was planned and filed. ATC's clearance can differ, so enter what ATC gives you here.
ofp.note: The filed SID is first in the route. Check it against your clearance.

sections.title: Takeoff
sections.sub: Numbers for the takeoff steps and the CDU's TAKEOFF REF page.

rows.label: Takeoff runway
rows.desc: Set in Clearance.

ofp.title: Takeoff speeds come from the FMC
ofp.body: The OFP plans the flight, not the takeoff. Speeds and trim come from the CDU's TAKEOFF REF page once weights and flaps are set. Some SimBrief layouts add takeoff performance at the end.
ofp.note: The FMC uses the takeoff weight for these speeds.

rows.label: Runway heading
rows.desc: The heading of your takeoff runway.

ofp.title: Takeoff speeds come from the FMC
ofp.body: The OFP plans the flight, not the takeoff. Speeds and trim come from the CDU's TAKEOFF REF page once weights and flaps are set. Some SimBrief layouts add takeoff performance at the end.
ofp.note: The FMC uses the takeoff weight for these speeds.

rows.label: Flaps
rows.desc: Takeoff flaps for your weight and runway.
rows.loc: Enter on the CDU › TAKEOFF REF

ofp.title: Takeoff speeds come from the FMC
ofp.body: The OFP plans the flight, not the takeoff. Speeds and trim come from the CDU's TAKEOFF REF page once weights and flaps are set. Some SimBrief layouts add takeoff performance at the end.
ofp.note: The FMC uses the takeoff weight for these speeds.

rows.label: Takeoff thrust
rows.desc: The rating from your takeoff performance in the EFB. TO is full thrust; TO-1 and TO-2 are fixed derates that give less.
rows.loc: Enter on the CDU › N1 LIMIT

ofp.title: Takeoff speeds come from the FMC
ofp.body: The OFP plans the flight, not the takeoff. Speeds and trim come from the CDU's TAKEOFF REF page once weights and flaps are set. Some SimBrief layouts add takeoff performance at the end.
ofp.note: The FMC uses the takeoff weight for these speeds.

rows.label: Assumed temperature (SEL)
rows.desc: From your takeoff performance in the EFB. A temperature hotter than the real one, so the FMC sets less thrust and saves the engines.
rows.loc: Enter on the CDU › N1 LIMIT

ofp.title: Takeoff speeds come from the FMC
ofp.body: The OFP plans the flight, not the takeoff. Speeds and trim come from the CDU's TAKEOFF REF page once weights and flaps are set. Some SimBrief layouts add takeoff performance at the end.
ofp.note: The FMC uses the takeoff weight for these speeds.

rows.label: V1
rows.desc: Decision speed. Before it you can stop; after it you go.
rows.loc: Enter on the CDU › TAKEOFF REF

ofp.title: Takeoff speeds come from the FMC
ofp.body: The OFP plans the flight, not the takeoff. Speeds and trim come from the CDU's TAKEOFF REF page once weights and flaps are set. Some SimBrief layouts add takeoff performance at the end.
ofp.note: The FMC uses the takeoff weight for these speeds.

rows.label: VR
rows.desc: Rotation speed.
rows.loc: Enter on the CDU › TAKEOFF REF

ofp.title: Takeoff speeds come from the FMC
ofp.body: The OFP plans the flight, not the takeoff. Speeds and trim come from the CDU's TAKEOFF REF page once weights and flaps are set. Some SimBrief layouts add takeoff performance at the end.
ofp.note: The FMC uses the takeoff weight for these speeds.

rows.label: V2
rows.desc: Takeoff safety speed for your takeoff flaps.
rows.loc: Enter on the CDU › TAKEOFF REF

ofp.title: Takeoff speeds come from the FMC
ofp.body: The OFP plans the flight, not the takeoff. Speeds and trim come from the CDU's TAKEOFF REF page once weights and flaps are set. Some SimBrief layouts add takeoff performance at the end.
ofp.note: The FMC uses the takeoff weight for these speeds.

rows.label: Stabilizer trim
rows.desc: Takeoff trim for your weight and balance.
rows.loc: Enter on the CDU › TAKEOFF REF

ofp.title: Takeoff speeds come from the FMC
ofp.body: The OFP plans the flight, not the takeoff. Speeds and trim come from the CDU's TAKEOFF REF page once weights and flaps are set. Some SimBrief layouts add takeoff performance at the end.
ofp.note: The FMC uses the takeoff weight for these speeds.

sections.title: Approach
sections.sub: Used by the Descent and Approach steps and the approach briefing. Arrival values live only here.

rows.label: Arrival runway
rows.desc: The runway you expect to land on. Check it against the ATIS before you brief.

ofp.title: The arrival runway and STAR end the route
ofp.body: The header's route line ends with the arrival: the STAR, then the destination and its runway. The destination's elevation is in the header too. Minimums and landing speed come from the approach chart and the FMC, not the OFP.
ofp.cap: Close-up, the end of the route
ofp.note: Check the planned runway against the ATIS before you brief; it often changes.

rows.label: Arrival (STAR)
rows.desc: The published route from the airway to the approach.

ofp.title: The arrival runway and STAR end the route
ofp.body: The header's route line ends with the arrival: the STAR, then the destination and its runway. The destination's elevation is in the header too. Minimums and landing speed come from the approach chart and the FMC, not the OFP.
ofp.cap: Close-up, the end of the route
ofp.note: Check the planned runway against the ATIS before you brief; it often changes.

rows.label: Transition level
rows.desc: Where you set the altimeters to the local setting on the way down.

ofp.title: The transition level is in the header
ofp.body: The header has the flight number, the airports, the route as filed, the distance and the times.
ofp.note: The destination's transition level.

rows.label: Minimums
rows.desc: The height where you must see the runway to continue, from the approach chart. BARO for most approaches; RADIO when the chart gives a radio altimeter height.

ofp.title: Minimums come from the approach chart
ofp.body: Minimums come from the approach chart, and the landing speed and flaps from the CDU's APPROACH REF page. The OFP doesn't print them.
ofp.cap: Close-up, the end of the route
ofp.note: The arrival in the plan is where these values apply.

rows.label: Landing speed
rows.desc: VREF for your landing flaps, plus any wind additive.
rows.loc: Enter on the CDU › APPROACH REF

ofp.title: Landing speed comes from the FMC
ofp.body: Minimums come from the approach chart, and the landing speed and flaps from the CDU's APPROACH REF page. The OFP doesn't print them.
ofp.cap: Close-up, the end of the route
ofp.note: The arrival in the plan is where these values apply.

rows.label: Landing flaps
rows.desc: The flaps you land with. Landing speed is VREF for this setting.
rows.loc: Enter on the CDU › APPROACH REF

ofp.title: Landing flaps come from the FMC
ofp.body: Minimums come from the approach chart, and the landing speed and flaps from the CDU's APPROACH REF page. The OFP doesn't print them.
ofp.cap: Close-up, the end of the route
ofp.note: The arrival in the plan is where these values apply.

rows.label: Autobrake
rows.desc: How hard the brakes apply on touchdown.

ofp.title: Autobrake is your choice for the runway
ofp.body: Minimums come from the approach chart, and the landing speed and flaps from the CDU's APPROACH REF page. The OFP doesn't print them.
ofp.cap: Close-up, the end of the route
ofp.note: The arrival in the plan is where these values apply.

rows.label: Landing altitude
rows.desc: The destination field elevation, from the plan.
rows.loc: Set on the pressurization panel › LAND ALT

ofp.title: The destination elevation is in the header
ofp.body: The header's route line ends with the arrival: the STAR, then the destination and its runway. The destination's elevation is in the header too. Minimums and landing speed come from the approach chart and the FMC, not the OFP.
ofp.cap: Close-up, the end of the route
ofp.note: The header gives each airport's elevation.
